app.name: HubSpot
app.canDo: Read and update contacts and other CRM records in the HubSpot accounts that users connect.

oauth.notes: On the current HubSpot developer platform, you build apps as 'projects' with the HubSpot CLI.

verdict.summary: You do not need approval to start. But you build the app with a command-line tool, not a web form. Until HubSpot lists your app on its Marketplace, users who install it must accept an 'unverified app' warning.

whoYouNeed.role: A person with a HubSpot developer account
whoYouNeed.why: This person creates and uploads the app from the developer account with the HubSpot CLI.

whoYouNeed.role: A Super Admin in the HubSpot account of each customer
whoYouNeed.why: In HubSpot, only Super Admins can install apps.

steps.title: Sign in to the HubSpot developer account and the CLI
steps.plain: Sign in to your HubSpot developer account. Then connect the HubSpot command-line tool to the account.
steps.technical: Install @hubspot/cli, version 7.6.0 or later. Run `hs account auth`. When the tool asks, paste the personal access key.
steps.whyHuman: You must sign in yourself. You must also paste the access key yourself.

steps.title: Create the app project
steps.plain: The agent runs one command. The command creates the files of the app. The agent selects OAuth, so that many HubSpot accounts can connect.
steps.technical: Run `hs project create` > App. Select distribution: marketplace and auth: oauth. Set a unique `uid` in app-hsmeta.json. If you change the uid later, HubSpot creates a different app.

steps.title: Add the callback address and permissions
steps.plain: In the settings file of the app, add the callback address of your app. Add the HubSpot permissions that your agent needs.
steps.technical: In `app-hsmeta.json`, set `auth.type: "oauth"`, `auth.redirectUrls: [<your callback URL>]` and `auth.requiredScopes: ["crm.objects.contacts.read", ...]`. Production redirect URLs must use https.

steps.title: Upload the app
steps.plain: The agent uploads the project. HubSpot then builds the app.

steps.title: Keep the client ID and secret in your app
steps.plain: Open the app in HubSpot and go to the Auth tab. Keep the client ID and secret in the secret store or environment variables of your app.
steps.technical: Run `hs project open`. Go to Project Components > your app > Auth > Client credentials.
steps.whyHuman: The secret is the password for your app. Paste it yourself. Then it does not go into the chat history of an agent.

steps.title: Install the app in a test account
steps.plain: Install the app in a HubSpot test account through the sign-in of your app. The app is not on the Marketplace yet. Thus, you must select a box to accept an 'unverified app'.
steps.whyHuman: A Super Admin of the account must install the app. A person must decide to accept the unverified-app warning.

steps.title: Use the access token directly (only your own account)
steps.plain: A private app on your own account has no sign-in steps. Copy the access token of the app. Keep it in the secret store or environment variables of your app.
steps.technical: In app-hsmeta.json, set auth.type to "static" and remove redirectUrls. Run hs project upload. Then copy the access token from the Auth tab of the app.
steps.whyHuman: The token is the password for your account. Paste it yourself.

forks.condition: You want to remove the 'unverified' warning (Marketplace listing)
forks.effect: You need at least 3 active installs in HubSpot accounts that are not related to you. HubSpot does a first review in 10 business days or less. All the feedback can take a maximum of 60 days.

forks.condition: Only the HubSpot account of your company will connect
forks.effect: Use a private app with a static token, not OAuth. You do not need callback addresses.

nuances.title: Only Super Admins can install
nuances.detail: A usual HubSpot user at your customer cannot connect the app.
nuances.ifStuck: Tell the HubSpot Super Admin of the customer to do the first connection.

nuances.title: Is there a maximum number of installs before the listing?
nuances.detail: Older HubSpot pages gave a small maximum number of installs for unlisted apps. The current pages that we read do not give a maximum.
nuances.ifStuck: Before you give an unlisted app to many customers, ask HubSpot developer support.

evidence.note: The current pages do not say this. We did not test it.

nuances.title: Access tokens last 30 minutes
nuances.detail: HubSpot access tokens expire after 1,800 seconds. Your code must use the refresh token to get a new access token.
nuances.ifStuck: If calls fail approximately 30 minutes after sign-in, make sure that your code gets a new token.

config.redirectUriNote: Add your callback address to `auth.redirectUrls` in `app-hsmeta.json`.

useCases.label: Work in the HubSpot accounts of your customers
useCases.summary: You build the app with the HubSpot CLI. HubSpot does not review it. Users who install it must accept an 'unverified app' warning until you list it on the Marketplace.

useCases.label: Only the HubSpot account of your company
useCases.summary: Use a private app with a static token. You do not need an OAuth redirect.

composio.note: Users can connect today through the Composio HubSpot app. Use it while you set up your own app or wait for the review. Users see 'Composio' on the approval screen. Other Composio customers share the same rate limits. Polling triggers run a maximum of one time in 15 minutes. Change to your own app when it is ready.

existingApp.summary: If the callback address of your agent is different, add it to `auth.redirectUrls` in `app-hsmeta.json`. Run `hs project upload`. Use the existing client ID and secret.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: You change the uid of the app
reReviewTriggers.effect: HubSpot then sees a different app. Existing installs do not move to it. Do not change the uid.
Accounts that installed the app must install it again to give the new scopes.

evidence.note: The pages that we read do not say this.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: Your app is on the HubSpot Marketplace
reReviewTriggers.effect: The HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team reviews changes to the listing again.

evidence.note: This is our conclusion from the listing process. The pages do not say this about changes.

blockers.symptom: You cannot list your app on the App Marketplace yet
blockers.cause: A listing needs at least three active installs. Each install must be a HubSpot account that is not related to your company. Each account must make successful API calls through your app in the last 30 days.
blockers.fix: First, use your install link to install the app in three customer accounts. Keep these accounts active. Then send the app for listing.

blockers.symptom: HubSpot sets your listing back to Draft or refuses it
blockers.cause: These are the usual causes: listing data that is missing, wrong or misleading, links that do not work, or scopes that your app requests but does not use.
blockers.fix: Do the changes that the Ecosystem Quality team asks for. Remove the scopes that you do not use, or make them optional. Send the app again. The first review takes a maximum of 10 business days. All the review must be complete in 60 days. Send one app at a time. HubSpot automatically refuses more applications.
